NLTK: 5 canonical advisories for C-extension path bypass, corpus symlinks and parser CPU exhaustion

5 canonical advisories fixed in NLTK 3.10.4: `BllipParser` passes caller-supplied model paths to the native `bllipparser` C extension without `pathsec` validation, enabling arbitrary file read (CVE-2026-126295); `YCOECorpusReader` performs only lexical path checks on `psd`/`pos` directories and follows symlinks outside the corpus root (CVE-2026-126304); and unbounded or quadratic CPU consumption affects `SteppingRecursiveDescentParser.parse()` (CVE-2026-126303), `TreebankWordTokenizer.span_tokenize` (CVE-2026-126300), and `LegalitySyllableTokenizer.tokenize` (GHSA-gpwc-27cw-rh9r).

What to checkUpgrade `nltk` to 3.10.4. Audit code paths that pass untrusted model paths, corpus archives, grammars or long tokens to these parsers and tokenizers.

SvelteKit: 4 advisories for adapter route-config injection and Node server crashes

4 SvelteKit advisories: an unhandled URIError crash when `reroute` rewrites malformed percent-encoded paths (CVE-2026-128117 in `@sveltejs/kit`), prerendered paths interpreted as regular expressions in generated Vercel routing configs (CVE-2026-128121 in `adapter-vercel` and `adapter-static`), arbitrary redirect rule injection into Cloudflare `_redirects` during prerendering (CVE-2026-128122 in `adapter-cloudflare`), and an `adapter-node` crash when mutating headers on immutable requests proxied via `fetch` (CVE-2026-128123).

Nuxt: leading `//` path bypasses server middleware and parent lockfiles widen dev workspaceDir

In `@nuxt/nitro-server` 4.6.0 through 4.6.3, a request path starting with `//` (such as `//x/admin`) is parsed as a URL with a host before page rendering and renders `/admin`, whereas Nitro routing, route rules, and `server/middleware` see `//x/admin` and skip checks keyed on `/admin` (CVE-2026-128077, incomplete fix for GHSA-9v7c-q64q-vv33). Separately, `@nuxt/schema` (CVE-2026-128070) can select a parent directory containing a stray lockfile or workspace file as `workspaceDir`, exposing parent files via the Vite dev server `/_nuxt/@fs/` endpoint.

What to checkUpgrade `@nuxt/nitro-server` and `@nuxt/schema` to 4.6.4. Review access controls that rely on path-prefix matching in `server/middleware` and verify dev-server directory boundaries.

Astro: case-variant sibling directory read in @astrojs/node image endpoint and dynamic-tag attribute injection

In CVE-2026-126364, the `/_image` endpoint in `@astrojs/node` used a case-insensitive path comparison when checking whether a local image was inside the output directory, allowing reads of files from sibling directories differing only in letter case on case-sensitive filesystems such as Linux. In the GHSA table, `astro` is patched in 7.4.7 while `@astrojs/node` (<= 11.1.11) has `first_patched_version` set to null. CVE-2026-126361 is an attribute injection (XSS) flaw where `/` is not stripped from dynamic tag names, fixed in 7.4.5.

What to checkUpgrade `astro` to 7.4.7 or later. Do not invent a patched version number for `@astrojs/node` where the GHSA record leaves `first_patched_version` null; check `/_image` exposure, sibling directory layout on case-sensitive filesystems, and untrusted input in dynamic tag names.

OpenTelemetry (JS / Go / Python): unredacted server-span query strings, attribute-length bypass and header parsing

In JavaScript, `@opentelemetry/instrumentation-http` (CVE-2026-128080) redacts sensitive URL query parameters on outgoing client spans but writes the raw query string verbatim into `url.query` on incoming server spans, exposing presigned URLs, SAS tokens and API keys in telemetry backends. In Go, valid U+FFFD runes bypass `AttributeValueLengthLimit` (CVE-2026-128085) and W3C baggage parsing causes disproportionate memory allocation (CVE-2026-128086). In Python, `opentelemetry-api` (CVE-2026-126360) suffers quadratic-time ReDoS on crafted `traceparent` headers.

What to checkUpgrade `@opentelemetry/instrumentation-http` to 0.222.0, the affected OpenTelemetry-Go modules (`sdk`, `sdk/log`, `trace`, `baggage`, `propagation`) to 1.47.0, and Python `opentelemetry-api` to 1.45.2. Check stored server spans for exposed `url.query` secrets and rotate any leaked tokens.

AutoMapper: MaxDepth is bypassed through constructor parameters and polymorphic maps, causing StackOverflow

Both default (64) and explicit `MaxDepth` limits added for CVE-2026-32933 were not enforced when recursion flows through constructor parameters such as positional `record` types (CVE-2026-128082) or across polymorphic and related mapping paths (CVE-2026-128081), allowing deeply nested inputs to trigger an uncatchable `StackOverflowException` and terminate the process.

What to checkUpgrade NuGet `AutoMapper` to 15.1.4 (for 15.x) or 16.3.0 (for 16.x), and enforce input nesting depth limits before mapping untrusted structures.

russh: kex_done callback runs before host-key verification and try_sign can sign after agent lock

In `russh` 0.55.0 through 0.65.0 (CVE-2026-128087), the `client::Handler::kex_done()` callback runs with the shared secret before host-key verification completes even when the server host key is rejected. In CVE-2026-128088 specific to 0.65.0, `try_sign()` holds an `Arc<PrivateKey>` and can complete signing without re-checking if another connection locks the agent during the await.

What to checkUpgrade the Rust `russh` crate to 0.65.1. Review applications that perform side effects inside `kex_done()` or use confirmation-constrained keys with SSH agent forwarding.

rails-html-sanitizer: concurrent scrubber state sharing enables XSS alongside SVG attribute ReDoS

`Rails::HTML::SafeListSanitizer` (both HTML4 and HTML5 variants) shares 1 `PermitScrubber` across concurrent `sanitize` calls on the same instance without synchronization, so interleaved calls passing different `tags:` or `attributes:` options can overwrite each other's allowlists and permit XSS (CVE-2026-128069). Separately, CVE-2026-128068 causes quadratic-time ReDoS when checking SVG `href` and `xlink:href` attributes containing long whitespace and newlines.

What to checkUpgrade RubyGems `rails-html-sanitizer` to 1.7.2 and review multi-threaded applications (such as Puma workers) that pass per-call `tags:` or `attributes:` overrides to `sanitize`.

By advisory: affected and fixed versions (2 advisories)

Laravel: user-controlled stdout inside Concurrency::run() process tasks can forge result messages

When application code inside `Concurrency::run()` (using the default `process` driver) prints user-controlled text directly to standard output, an attacker can forge the framework's internal result message and reach code execution in the parent process (CVE-2026-128083). This requires a route reaching `Concurrency::run()` that outputs untrusted input.

What to checkUpgrade Composer `laravel/framework` to 12.71.0 (12.x) or 13.40.0 (13.x) and avoid printing raw user input inside concurrent tasks.

sqlite3-ruby: SQL strings of 4 GiB or larger wrap when cast to 32-bit int, truncating trailing clauses

On 64-bit platforms, the Ruby SQLite binding cast Ruby string lengths (`long`) to `int` before passing them to SQLite, causing strings of 4 GiB (2^32 bytes) or larger to wrap and potentially drop trailing SQL clauses such as `WHERE` (CVE-2026-128084).

What to checkUpgrade RubyGems `sqlite3` to 2.10.2 and bound input sizes before constructing SQL queries.

GitHub reviewed advisory API — saved publication window

11/13 18:25–11/14 09:00 JST NVD publication window / retrieval-time revision · Review publication & updates

FrankenPHP, NocoDB and OpenEMR: stale base-image Docker tags, PostgreSQL Viewer SQLi and FHIR OAuth bypass

3 NVD additions in this window: FrankenPHP Docker images before 1.1.11 were rebuilt only when new base-image tags appeared, leaving existing tags with unpatched Alpine, PHP and Go libraries such as `libcrypto3` CVE-2025-15467 (CVE-2026-128027); NocoDB before 2026.08.0 allows authenticated Viewer users on PostgreSQL to read other tables and hidden columns via SQL injection in the legacy `where` parameter (CVE-2026-126285); and OpenEMR before 8.4.0 allows unauthenticated callers to register `system:Patient.read` and request `system/Patient.write` for unapproved FHIR access (CVE-2026-126473).

What to checkPull and redeploy FrankenPHP 1.1.11+ by digest, upgrade NocoDB to 2026.08.0+, and upgrade OpenEMR to 8.4.0+. Verify library versions inside running containers rather than relying on mutable Docker tag names.

NVD published CVE records

11/13 18:25–11/14 09:00 JST NVD publication window / retrieval-time revision · Review publication & updates

BuildPiper, Tactical RMM and Keep: k8s escalation, WeasyPrint NATS key read and CEL-to-SQL injection

OpsTree BuildPiper before 2.7.0 allows project or deploy users to gain `cluster-admin` via unrestricted Additional Manifests (CVE-2026-127073) or mount the worker root filesystem via arbitrary `hostPath` volumes (CVE-2026-127080). Tactical RMM 0.17.0 through 1.6.1 (CVE-2026-129165) resolves `file://` links in WeasyPrint report previews, letting users with report-management permission read the Django `SECRET_KEY` (reused as the NATS password) and push `runscript` commands to managed agents. Keep 0.34.10 through 0.55.0 (CVE-2026-129166) has a blind SQL injection in its CEL-to-SQL converter. NVD does not list fixed versions for the latter 2 records.

What to checkUpgrade BuildPiper to 2.7.0+ and enforce Kubernetes admission policies on `ClusterRoleBinding` and `hostPath`. Do not invent fixed version numbers for Tactical RMM or Keep from NVD text; restrict report-preview and NATS access and audit CEL query exposure.

npm: 693 malicious-package advisories and affected versions preserved

Preserves the 693 publication-window advisories with individual GHSA IDs, package names and version ranges. Advisory counts are not unique package counts, execution counts or victim counts. Do not infer a safe upgrade target when no patched version is listed.

What to checkInspect lockfiles, caches and CI history for installation/execution of affected packages and versions. When affected, isolate, investigate secrets and artifacts and revoke exposed credentials. Deletion does not undo previous execution.

11/13 21:31 UTC Microsoft publication / current text at retrieval · Review publication & updates

ScreenConnect / SCKit: RMM+ empty-key condition and RelayTrap reverse spread to technician workstations

Microsoft published its analysis of SCKit and RelayTrap on 11/13. It separates 2 distinct attack surfaces: the reported server-side entry via RMM+ extensions (where versions 1.0.31 and 1.0.32 accepted an empty access key when none was configured) and the client-side RelayTrap path that delivers a payload from a compromised customer endpoint to a connecting technician workstation (blocked by the CVE-2026-84869 fix in client 26.6.5+). SCKit silently installs a separate client tied to attacker infrastructure and persists via scheduled tasks and registry Run entries.

What to checkRemoving an unauthorized ScreenConnect client alone does not clear scheduled-task or registry Run persistence or invalidate hijacked web sessions. Verify every technician client is at 26.6.5+, keep affected RMM+ extensions disabled, and investigate both technician workstations and downstream customer endpoints to revoke sessions and remove persistence.

Microsoft Security Blog SCKit analysis / ConnectWise Trust Center advisory

11/13 KEV addition & 11/08 oss-security advisory / retrieval-time revision · Review publication & updates

UnrealIRCd: added to KEV, label-tag newline injection executes commands with server authority

CISA added CVE-2026-114713 to KEV on 11/13 (due 11/16). On a network with 2 or more linked servers, injecting newlines into the IRCv3 labeled-response (label) tag inserts arbitrary commands into server-to-server traffic, allowing an ordinary user to run KILL, GLINE and other actions with server or IRCOp authority. Release 6.2.7.1 and hot-patch bundle-20261107 fix this critical flaw and decloak or DoS issues (9 fixes in total).

What to checkOn 6.0.0 through 6.2.7, apply `./unrealircd hot-patch bundle-20261107` and verify `5.0-hot-patch-bundle-20261107` via `./unrealircd module-status|grep labeled-response`, or upgrade to 6.2.7.1 and restart. The temporary SPAMFILTER on 6.0.4+ does not fix the other 8 flaws. EOL series 5 requires `blacklist-module "labeled-response";` and a full restart (rehash is insufficient), though continuing to run an EOL release is not safe.

CISA KEV catalog / Openwall oss-security UnrealIRCd advisory / NVD modified CVE record

11/13 KEV addition & 11/12 sk1000362 revision / retrieval-time revision · Review publication & updates

Check Point DynamicCLI: added to KEV, root privilege escalation via 0777 local socket

CISA added CVE-2026-123039 to KEV on 11/13 (due 11/16). On Gaia OS, the root `dynamic_server` process listens on `/tmp/dynamic_socket` with world-writable (0777) permissions and no peer authentication, allowing an attacker with existing local execution to run arbitrary commands as root. Check Point observed active exploitation against a couple of dozen customers. Spark Firewalls and Smart-1 Cloud are unaffected.

What to checkApply the Jumbo Hotfix Accumulator (R82.20 Take 14, R82.10 Take 52, R82 Take 132, or R81.20 Take 174 and later) and verify `ls -l /tmp/dynamic_socket` shows `srw-rw---- root config (0660)` rather than `0777`. Stopping `dynamic_server` via `dbset process:dynamic_server` and `dbset :save` mitigates the socket exposure but breaks sk144112 Dynamic CLI commands. Audit `/var/log/dynamicCli.log` for `Received =` lines missing the Clish wrapper and for `Rejected connection from unauthorized uid`.

CISA KEV catalog / Check Point sk1000362 advisory / NVD modified CVE record

11/13 oss-security & NVD publication / retrieval-time revision · Review publication & updates

Apache APISIX: 7 flaws across identity headers, path normalization and openapi-to-mcp boundaries

7 vulnerabilities fixed in Apache APISIX 3.20.0: client-supplied identity headers survive when multi-auth falls back from wolf-rbac (CVE-2026-124666, 3.8.0–3.19.0) or when jwe-decrypt uses `strict: false` or forward-auth uses `allow_degradation: true` (CVE-2026-124679, 3.18.0–3.19.0); encoded dot-segment mismatches bypass route-level auth on shared upstreams (CVE-2026-124680, 0.9–3.19.0); authz-keycloak grants access when holding any single required scope including denied HTTP methods (CVE-2026-124716, 1.4.0–3.19.0); combining `match_uri_encoded_slash` and `skip_mtls_uri_regex` bypasses mTLS on paths decoding to exempted URIs (CVE-2026-124723, 3.18.0–3.19.0); and openapi-to-mcp allows caller identity spoofing and relative path traversal to undeclared API endpoints (CVE-2026-124719 and CVE-2026-124726, 3.19.0).

What to checkUpgrade Apache APISIX to 3.20.0. Audit route plugin configurations (`strict: false`, `allow_degradation: true`, `match_uri_encoded_slash`, and `openapi-to-mcp`) and verify whether upstream services blindly trust caller-supplied identity headers.

11/13 oss-security disclosure / text at retrieval, no fixed version yet · Review publication & updates

Dropbear SSH: authorized_keys permitopen/permitlisten restrictions are not enforced on Unix-socket forwarding

Disclosed on oss-security on 11/13 (no CVE assigned yet, verified at commit 99baf182). In `authorized_keys`, `permitopen="host:port"` and `permitlisten="host:port"` are checked on TCP forwarding (`svr-tcpfwd.c`), whereas default-enabled Unix domain socket forwarding (`direct-streamlocal@openssh.com` / `streamlocal-forward@openssh.com` in `svr-streamfwd.c`) checks only `no-port-forwarding` and ignores destination limits. If a CI or deploy account with a restricted key belongs to the `docker` group or similar, it can reach `/var/run/docker.sock` or database sockets. This is not an unauthenticated flaw.

What to checkNo upstream fixed release is available yet. Do not rely on `permitopen` or `permitlisten` alone to isolate accounts from local Unix sockets; add `no-port-forwarding` where forwarding is unneeded or remove restricted-key accounts from the `docker` group and sensitive socket permissions.

oss-sec Dropbear streamlocal disclosure

Continued review of the 10/26 bulletin and 10/27 tag / prior context; prose not revalidated in this review / Text not revalidated in this update · Publication or update confirmed

Tailscale: minimum fixed version 1.104.4 for 4 official advisories

TS-2026-014–017 concern SSH Unix socket forwarding, SSH memory DoS, Serve Unix backends, and HTTP/2 capability confusion. The official bulletin specifies at least 1.104.4. A timing gap in changelog updates remains. Do not equate this with fixes for all 11 Tailworm items.

What to checkVerify 1.104.4 or later on production clients and check SSH/Serve usage conditions. To temporarily disable SSH forwarding, set TS_SSH_DISABLE_FORWARDING=1 and restart the daemon. Do not include headscale or experimental connectors in the same fix scope.

Revised 10/27 23:45 JST / prior context; prose not revalidated in this review / Text not revalidated in this update · Publication or update confirmed

Fireblocks mpc-lib: still no fix after assessment revision.

CERT VU701544 was revised on the 27th at 14:45 UTC. Descendant shares and chain codes may permit access to ancestor/root shares of the same MPC party, but this is not equivalent to obtaining a complete transfer key exceeding the threshold. Actual theft, amounts, and affected customer counts have not been disclosed.

What to checkTreat the fix as unavailable, protect chain codes as secrets, and investigate the entire hierarchy. Do not reuse Agent2.4.4 / SDK2.19.1 from the separate eMudhra incident as fixed versions for this vulnerability.

CERT VU701544

CVE-2026-41709 concerns actions left unlogged after administrator access, with a deadline of 11/11. Addition dates are not attack start dates; deadlines are requirements for US federal agencies.

2026-10-29 / review / Text not revalidated in this update · Publication or update confirmed

From PHP to the kernel and identity systems: observed artifacts and uncertainty

Dream’s report dated 10/26 describes artifacts of PHP2Shell chained with CVE-2026-46300 to gain root on 25 servers: 24 firewalls and an additional management server. It reports decrypted LDAP credentials and enumeration, but explicitly cannot determine whether password spraying, backdoor account creation or SAML key extraction succeeded. These are researcher observations without independent victim confirmation; direct evidence of AI code generation is also absent.

What to checkRestrict exposed management interfaces and update. Where compromise is suspected, investigate management servers, LDAP credentials, tunnels and identity logs. Do not infer undisclosed product names or affected versions.

Dream Research / CISA KEV

So-net: member information and some email passwords exposed

The official 10/27 notice says access on 10/19 was detected on 23 and disclosure established on 24. It separately reports 2,141,986 So-net member records and 443,495 plala (S course) member records. The notice also reports 16 bank-account records and 7 notification records. Do not add these as a count of people.

Struts REST: any-setter requires configuration as well as an update

In Struts 2 versions 7.2.1–7.3.0, @StrutsParameter restrictions do not cover REST @JsonAnySetter members. 2026-10-31T20:17:11.191Z / Apache CNA publication; NVD registration at 21:16:53 UTC / Historical context; not rereviewed in this window · Publication/update confirmed

Apache MINA 3.0 codec: deserialization from untrusted peers

The Apache CNA describes CVE-2026-118636: JavaNativeMessageDecoder calls ObjectInputStream.readObject() without a class filter, allowing gadget-chain RCE in applications that expose this decoder to untrusted peers. The 3.0 branch is inactive, no fixed release is planned, and the latest 2.2.X branch is recommended. NVD registration was on 10/31 at 21:16:53 UTC; this is not confirmation of exploitation.

What to checkCheck use of the affected codec and reachability from external peers; prevent untrusted input from reaching it. Rather than waiting for a 3.0 fix, assess compatibility and migrate to the latest 2.2.X branch. Check the original affected-version fields against your artifacts.

privacypass-py: credential exfiltration during build, install and import

The Amazon Inspector record reports code posing as cryptographic primitives that sends host information and credential-bearing environment variables externally during build or install and again at import. The import path also runs outside pip build isolation. The name does not establish compromise of the legitimate Privacy Pass project.

What to checkCheck installation and import history for affected versions. Isolate affected environments and revoke and replace credentials from another environment. Do not rely only on build isolation or contact the reported collection endpoint to test it.

Northflank: reports of unauthorized AI API key use and secret rotation

The official status page discloses user reports of unauthorized AI API key use. Within this window, audit logs were opened to all customers and secret rotation was announced for MySQL, Redis, Minio and RabbitMQ. The precautionary instruction to assume all environment variables were decrypted is not confirmation that every variable was leaked.

What to checkRevoke keys at their issuer, issue replacements and update workloads. Review AI usage, billing and audit logs, and rotate database secrets. Availability of rotation features does not establish completion by customers or full service recovery.

2026-11-01T12:33:30Z – 2026-11-03T07:20:00Z / GHSA publication window / Historical context; not rereviewed in this window · Publication/update confirmed

DBHub: MySQL/MariaDB read-only bypass fixed in 0.22.6

In @bytebase/dbhub below 0.22.6, different SQL comment interpretation can bypass the MySQL/MariaDB connector read-only check. An actor able to influence SQL sent by an AI can reach writes or DDL when database permissions allow them. PostgreSQL is outside this path.

What to checkUpdate to 0.22.6 or later and also restrict the database account to read-only access. Check AI inputs, connection privileges and audit logs. Updating does not establish that earlier writes never occurred.

SD-JWT: silently discarded disclosures can change authorization

CVE-2026-62374 silently discards mismatched Disclosures and returns success. A valid signature can accompany fewer claims, affecting verifiers that allow access when a constraining claim is absent. Required key binding rejects on-path tampering; tampering by the holder remains a distinct condition.

What to check@sd-jwt/core through 0.19.0 is affected, with 0.20.0 listed as the first fix. @sd-jwt/decode through 0.19.0 is affected but has no first fix listed. Reject missing required claims and verify each deployed dependency separately.

The advisory reports cross-database reads by authenticated tokens through DuckDB I/O aliases within the shared storage root. Its prose describes an unresolved issue including 26.06.2, while the structured API names a fix-equivalent commit version; these claims conflict.

Affected configurations enable client uploads in @payloadcms/storage-vercel-blob and let authenticated users access the upload route. Configurations without client uploads are outside this path.

odf-kit: XSS through style attributes in converted documents

odtToHtml() and odsToHtml() interpolate unescaped style values. Inserting the output from a crafted document as HTML can execute script. Versions from 0.6.0 up to but excluding 0.14.2 are affected.

What to checkUpgrade to 0.14.2 or later and avoid directly displaying HTML from untrusted documents. Review previously converted output too.

2026-11-03T20:29:16Z / GHSA publication / Prior context retained; narrative not rereviewed in this update · Publication/update confirmed

Stanza: nested pickle escapes weights_only checks

The lemmatizer in 1.14.0 performs unrestricted deserialization of compressed pickle inside a model. The advisory reports code execution as the loading user from an attacker-supplied lemma .pt. torch.load with weights_only=True does not inspect that inner pickle.

What to checkUpgrade to 1.15.0 and reject models of unknown origin. Investigate execution history and credential exposure in environments that already loaded them.

Elo: constructor access in JavaScript output

An attacker-controlled Elo string can reach host code execution when generated JavaScript is executed through unfiltered constructor access. This differs from the separate advisory about directly supplied AST objects.

What to checkUpgrade @enspirit/elo to 1.0.1. Do not execute code generated from untrusted input in a process with secrets or host privileges.

2026-11-03T17:51:30Z / GHSA publication / Prior context retained; narrative not rereviewed in this update · Publication/update confirmed

Elo: interpolation in generated Ruby

The Ruby backend does not sufficiently escape interpolation in emitted string literals and subtype-constraint labels. Running Ruby generated from crafted Elo can evaluate attacker-controlled expressions.

What to checkUpgrade @enspirit/elo to 1.0.1 and regenerate Ruby output. Safety of output from another backend does not establish safety of the Ruby output.

2026-11-03T17:48:09Z / GHSA publication / Prior context retained; narrative not rereviewed in this update · Publication/update confirmed

Elo: validation of programmatic AST input

Integrations that construct AST objects from JSON or plugins can pass unchecked fields into JavaScript, Ruby, Python or SQL output, enabling code injection. This input boundary differs from the normal string parser.

What to checkUpgrade @enspirit/elo to 1.0.1. Validate AST types and syntax and isolate generation and execution from untrusted ASTs.

  • @enspirit/elo (npm): affected <= 1.0.0 → fixed version 1.0.1

.NET Brotli: new indexing and existing remediation

This is a GHSA registration for the previously covered CVE-2026-111497. Exposure requires processing attacker-controlled Brotli data with decompression enabled; ASP.NET Core and HttpClient do not enable this automatically by default. .NET Framework is unaffected.

What to checkApply the fixed version for each branch and package in the table, including 8.0.33, 9.0.22 and 10.0.14. Republish NativeAOT with the updated toolchain and verify distributed artifacts.

praktor: Telegram uploads cross workspace boundaries

In 0.9.0 and earlier, a Telegram document filename can write outside uploads within the persistent agent workspace. Overwritten instruction or configuration files can affect subsequent runs. This is not proof of arbitrary writes across the host.

What to checkUpgrade to 0.9.1 and restrict allowed Telegram user IDs. Review instructions, skills, hooks and upload history in existing volumes.

Keycloak: signature verification bypass in JWT Authorization Grant

An attacker with valid client credentials can exploit algorithm confusion in the JWT Authorization Grant flow to bypass signature verification and issue tokens for federated users linked to the affected Identity Provider. This does not establish an attack without credentials against every user.

What to checkUpgrade keycloak-services to 26.6.4. Review the affected flow, Identity Provider and client credentials and investigate unauthorized token issuance.

Metalama: code execution through same-user named pipes

Unrestricted deserialization over Visual Studio inter-process pipes can execute code. Writing requires code execution as the same Windows user already; this does not establish privilege escalation. The prose says no backports, while the API also lists 2025.1.18 and 2026.0.25 as fixes; the conflict is retained.

What to checkCheck Metalama 2026.1.19 and the maintained PostSharp extension 2026.1.5. Remove or migrate retired extensions and cross-check advisory and shipped releases for older branches.

Arc: logs route registered before authentication middleware

The advisory reports unauthenticated access to recent application logs because /api/v1/logs is registered before authentication middleware even with authentication enabled. Internal paths and database names may leak; retrieval of the bootstrap admin token was not confirmed.

What to checkPlace the logs route behind authentication and administrator authorization or block it if unused. Verify artifacts contain the fix commit in the table and review sensitive data in stored logs.

2026-11-05T07:08:00Z – 2026-11-07T04:36:00Z / GHSA publication window / Prior context retained; narrative not rereviewed in this update · Publication/update confirmed

kaniko: Azure build tokens sent to lookalike registries

Untrusted Dockerfiles or build arguments can expose ARM access tokens when the build can obtain an Azure identity. Neither RUN nor push is required; using ACR is not a prerequisite. The fix is 1.25.20, but this repository publishes no binaries or images. The original acr-env module has no fixed release.

What to checkRebuild the executor, warmer and credential helper from 1.25.20 or later. Review Entra and Azure logs and identity permissions for suspect builds. Rotating credentials does not revoke issued tokens; investigate their remaining lifetime and any secrets the identity could read.

By advisory: affected and fixed versions (1 entry)

  • github.com/chainguard-dev/kaniko (go): affected < 1.25.20 → fixed version 1.25.20

LXD: restored snapshots bypass restricted-project controls

The advisory reports that imported snapshots bypass lowlevel-hook restrictions and can execute commands with host privileges. Transfer and restore capabilities are prerequisites; this does not establish unauthenticated RCE on every public API. The narrative cites Incus while the table describes LXD Go module boundaries.

What to checkAudit snapshot import, transfer and restore permissions and update the applicable vendor release line. Do not mechanically convert Go pseudo-versions into LXD distribution or Incus release numbers.

LXD: source authorization and DevLXD volume ownership

Cross-project instance and custom-volume copies check the destination without establishing permission to view the source. A separate DevLXD issue allows a guest with volume management enabled to read and write another guest’s volumes within the same project. These are different authorization boundaries.

What to checkReview copy permissions, source-project visibility and DevLXD volume-management settings. Restrict unnecessary guest permissions and investigate unexpected copies, device changes and secret access. Keep each advisory’s module boundary rather than reducing them to one release number.

LXD: backup-import crashes and compression arguments

An authenticated user allowed to create storage volumes can reportedly stop the daemon with a backup lacking snapshot expiry. A separate advisory covers extra compression arguments leading to host writes and possible code execution. An earlier nil-check patch does not establish that adjacent fields were fixed.

What to checkRestrict backup import and export permissions and inputs, and check the distinct fix boundaries below. Restarting the daemon is not a permanent fix; investigate potential host writes separately.

OSAC: kubeconfig exec plugins run inside the proxy pod

In remote or auto VM cluster mode, the attacker must be able to create or modify a labelled Secret in a namespace readable by the proxy. Its exec plugin runs with console-proxy pod privileges; the server URL is also an SSRF path. Local-only deployments are unaffected. The advisory names 0.0.4 while asking users to verify a release containing the patch.

What to checkRestrict Secret writes in the relevant namespace and verify that the deployed image contains the fix. Pod execution does not establish host root; investigate service-account permissions, destinations and Secret changes.

KEV: SonicOS SSLVPN SAML and MFA bypass added

The 11/6 KEV addition is CVE-2026-19868. A user with valid alternate-authentication credentials may bypass SAML controls and potentially SAML-enforced MFA. This is not a general credential-free MFA bypass. The retrieved official PSIRT page was only a JavaScript shell, so its body did not establish a minimum fixed version in this review.

What to checkCheck affected products, settings and fixes in the official SonicWall advisory and review alternate SSLVPN authentication and exposure. The KEV dueDate is 2026-11-20, not a legal deadline shared by every organization. Continue log review and credential assessment.

The records cover other-user access tokens and administrative control through hard-coded credentials. CVE-2026-16720 and CVE-2026-17403 affect 10.0.8.0–10.0.8.12 and 12.1.0.0–12.1.1.2. CVE-2026-17360 affects 12.1.0.0–12.1.1.2. IBM initially published on 11/5; 11/7 NVD registration is not attack onset.

2026-11-07T04:36:00Z – 2026-11-08T02:13:00Z / NVD publication window / Historical context; not rereviewed in this window · CNA record; preconditions require caution

Keycloak: client-management roles reach JavaScript policies

Session state during client creation or import with authorization services enabled permits inline JavaScript policy upload restrictions to be bypassed. Authenticated delegated client-management privileges are required. Red Hat lists CVSS 9.1 and Important, marks packages Affected and supplies no fixed release. Its public_date is 2026-01-07, differing from this NVD registration date.

What to checkReview delegated manage-clients permissions, client imports and policy changes. Track product-specific Red Hat fixes without inventing a release. Default script restrictions alone do not establish protection against this path.

2026-11-07T04:36:00Z – 2026-11-08T02:13:00Z / NVD publication window / Historical context; not rereviewed in this window · CNA record; preconditions require caution

Fiber Admin: error-page configuration and a race condition

Before 4.0.1, an enabled custom database error page and a race with an administrator saving settings allow a request header to be written into a PHP file. Authentication is not required, but configuration and race prerequisites matter. WPScan lists 4.0.1 as fixed and 11/5 as initial publication.

What to checkUpdate to a release containing the 4.0.1 fix and inspect the custom database error-page setting and generated PHP files. Disabling a feature is distinct from completed patch deployment; correlate settings changes with access logs.

2026-11-07T04:36:00Z – 2026-11-08T02:13:00Z / NVD publication window / Historical context; not rereviewed in this window · CNA record; preconditions require caution

LatePoint: reset-token values become SQL conditions

The NVD CNA description covers the booking plugin through 5.7.6: reset values can be treated as SQL conditions. Customer takeover exposes bookings and personal data, with linked WordPress accounts affected depending on configuration. The 5.7.5 scalar check is insufficient. Wordfence returned HTTP success with an empty body, so its text did not verify a fixed release.

What to checkCheck official LatePoint releases and CNA remediation guidance and verify the deployed fix. Do not assert a minimum fixed release from the bodies verified here. Investigate resets, customer-account changes and booking-data access.

The NVD CNA description reports a missing checkout-registration role allowlist through 1.1.4, permitting unauthenticated administrator escalation. My Account checks do not establish checkout safety. A changeset references 1.1.5, but Wordfence’s empty body does not verify a shipped fixed release.

OpenAM: notification WebSocket session-token exposure and SAML / self-registration authentication boundaries

In CVE-2026-123551 (from 14.0.0 before 16.1.4), an internal forward on legacy Liberty ID-FF endpoints reaches the notification WebSocket without authentication and exposes live iPlanetDirectoryPro tokens. In CVE-2026-123550 (before 16.1.4), ECP (PAOS) and HTTP-Artifact bindings accept unsigned assertions when WantAssertionsSigned is disabled. In CVE-2026-123549 (before 16.1.4), self-registration fails to enforce Valid Creation Attributes and permits joining administrative groups. The GitHub advisories were published on 10/22, distinct from this NVD registration date.

What to checkUpdate to 16.1.4 and inspect exposure of the notification WebSocket and Liberty ID-FF endpoints, SAML SP WantAssertionsSigned settings, and whether self-registration is enabled. Separate patch deployment from revoking and auditing existing sessions and unauthorized accounts.

CVE-2026-124469 (Fee Sheet ORDER BY SQL injection) and CVE-2026-124450 (arbitrary file read/write via disposeDocument in the fax/sms module) affect versions before 8.3.0 and are fixed in 8.3.0. By contrast, CVE-2026-124445 (OneTimeAuth token replay and PIN brute force from 7.0.1 before 8.4.0) and CVE-2026-124467 (chained RCE via ESign router LFI and fax upload before 8.4.0) are fixed in 8.4.0. Updating only to 8.3.0 does not resolve the issues fixed in 8.4.0. Initial GitHub advisory publication occurred in months 8 and 9.

What to checkVerify a release at 8.4.0 or later and do not conflate 8.3.0 fixes with 8.4.0 fixes. Check whether the fax/sms and ESign modules are enabled, and investigate suspicious access to sqlconf.php, temporary upload paths and patient-portal token usage.

AI/MCP: loopback trust, shell exposure and workspace boundaries

GPUStack loopback auto-admin can be reached through a same-host reverse proxy or forged header; fixed in 2.2.0, with reported exploitation and a KEV addition. fast-agent-mcp through 0.7.20 exposes unauthenticated HTTP; --shell adds RCE, fixed in 0.7.21. The macOS Claude Code Edit race requires attacker code inside the sandbox; fixed in 2.1.251. These advisories have independent conditions. This publication window contains 13 advisories.

What to checkUpgrade GPUStack to 2.2.0 or later and audit API keys and worker secrets. Check MCP binding, authentication and shell capabilities, and use each package table for fixes. Agent/workspace findings alone do not establish a compromised host.

Rucio: SSH challenges accepted as authentication tokens enable administrator impersonation

SSH challenges are nonces for a later key exchange, but are stored alongside authentication tokens and not distinguished during validation. An unauthenticated caller can request a challenge for an arbitrary account and use it within its short lifetime to access APIs as that account, including an administrator. Exact affected and fixed branches are retained below.

What to checkUpdate rucio to a fixed release on its branch: 35.9.1 / 38.6.1 / 40.4.2 / 41.1.1 or later. Review API exposure, authentication and privileged operations. Keep nonces separate from authenticated credentials.

Separate advisories cover SVG local-reference checks, URI schemes, escaped CSS URLs, HTML5 attribute sanitization and regex denial of service. Calling a sanitizer alone does not establish safety in every output context.

What to checkUpdate loofah to 2.25.3 and inspect selected scrubbers and HTML/SVG output contexts. Check output encoding and policy alongside the dependency update.

basic-ftp: process crashes from CR/LF and MLSD parsing

CR/LF in passwords or resumed-download paths and an MLSD __proto__ fact trigger separate unhandled-exception paths. Release 6.2.3 fixes the former but remains affected by the latter.

What to checkUpdate basic-ftp to 6.2.4. Review untrusted FTP listings and input handling; 6.2.3 alone does not fix both issues.

Signal K: unauthenticated WebSockets can subscribe to buffered logs

WebSockets intentionally allow pre-login connections, but log subscriptions omit the authorization checks used elsewhere and can replay buffered server logs. The advisory describes code review, not captured frames from a running server.

What to checkCheck the signalk-server fix in 2.31.0-beta.1 and its availability in the stable release you use. Review WebSocket exposure and sensitive information in logs.

GitHub malware API — saved publication window

11/12 18:45 UTC update / current retrieved text · Publication/update confirmed

ScreenConnect: separate technician-client protection from compromise remediation

ConnectWise’s 11/12 18:45 UTC update identifies approximately 400 environments with RMM+ extensions for precautionary action, not confirmed compromises. Its current assessment finds no evidence of compromised ConnectWise infrastructure or a ScreenConnect vulnerability in initial access. Clients at 26.6.5 or later block the SCKit endpoint-to-technician spread technique, but do not remove existing compromises.

What to checkVerify the installed client on every technician workstation is 26.6.5 or later; keep the identified extensions disabled. Revoke web/IdP sessions from a trusted device and investigate with independent EDR or other out-of-band tooling. Preserve evidence, then clear queued commands/Toolbox items, unauthorized clients and persistence; validate before reconnecting.

ConnectWise Trust Center advisory

11/12 publication / date only; retrieval-time text · Publication/update confirmed

Air Terminal 6: OS command injection requires management login

JVN published this on 11/12. On v1.01.80 and earlier, a user able to log in to the web administration interface can execute commands as root. This is not an unauthenticated Internet-wide condition. The developer says fixed firmware has been deployed and disconnected devices update automatically on reconnection, so no user action is required.

What to checkCheck the official automatic-update conditions and device connectivity. Do not invent a fixed firmware number, which JVN does not list. Limit unnecessary management-interface access and shared credentials.

JVN coordinated disclosure

11/12 affected-scope revision / first published 11/09 · Publication/update confirmed

KUSANAGI: the 11/12 revision clarifies Nginx redirect scope

JVN published on 11/09 and revised affected scope on 11/12. CRLF handling in WordPress Nginx redirect rules can inject response headers when a crafted URL is visited. Affected: all KUSANAGI 7; all 8 Free/Business/Premium; 9 Security/Enterprise through 10.7.2-1 and Free/Business/Premium through 9.12.2-1. Apache httpd configurations are excluded.

What to checkCheck the edition and Nginx configuration, then apply the developer’s latest update or official workaround. Keep Apache exclusions explicit and do not infer a minimum fixed version absent from JVN.

JVN scope revision

11/12 JVN publication / notice of Apache 11/11 update · Publication/update confirmed

Apache HTTP Server: verify release 2.4.71 and deployed binaries

JVN’s 11/12 notice announces Apache HTTP Server 2.4.71 for multiple issues in the 2.4 series. JVN delegates details to Apache advisories; this short notice alone does not establish every CVE prerequisite or exploitation status.

What to checkCheck official Apache advisories and distribution backports against enabled modules and running binaries. Distinguish an available update from the process running after restart.

JVN Apache update notice

Collection scope, overlap and limitations

673NVD new records
1,466NVD revisions
1,329GHSA publication window
78Verified saved and referenced responses

All 673 newly published NVD records overlap the 1466 modified records. GHSA published 1329 advisories (593 unreviewed, 697 malware) and modified 1544. Distinguish reviewed, unreviewed and malware categories and check publication/modification overlap in the register. KEV is at version 2026.11.13 with 1,781 entries, adding CVE-2026-114713 / CVE-2026-123039 over the prior saved catalog. Catalog additions differ from attack start dates, and absence from KEV is not proof of non-exploitation. Of 78 verified responses, 24 reference identical prior captures to avoid duplicate storage.

  • Counts describe database records and editorial topics, not attacks or victims. Do not add overlapping NVD/GHSA or publication/modification totals.
  • The prior 283 topics and 21 impact cases retain their historical context, and Check Point CVE-2026-123039 active exploitation is added as 1 bounded impact case (22 total). Historical entries were not re-audited in full.
  • API queries ran after cutoff. Publication, registration, modification and retrieval are distinct; retrieval-time bodies cannot reconstruct every earlier revision.
  • All 39 GHSA reviewed advisories (including 7 withdrawn NLTK duplicates kept separate) and 697 malware advisories preserve their raw package version tables. The 593 unreviewed advisories are retained in raw pages and indexes without claiming independent verification of every body.
  • KEV advanced to catalog 2026.11.13 with 1,781 entries and 2 additions (CVE-2026-114713 and CVE-2026-123039). The legacy IPA feed returned 404 (fallback succeeded), Feishu hit a redirect loop, and the php.net 2026 archive timed out.
  • Where upstream advisories or NVD records omit a fixed version (such as Dropbear streamlocal, `@astrojs/node`, Tactical RMM, or Keep), no patched release number is invented.
